**What stands out:** Collections are slow across the whole portfolio, and delivery is weak on the semiconductor accounts. **Infineon Technologies** is the clearest case where problems in several apps overlap.

  - SK Hynix ($773,085) and GlobalFoundries ($756,615) carry the highest late cost.
- **Infineon:** It is the only High credit-risk customer. It also has the most disputes (2) and the lowest OTIF. Poor delivery may be driving the disputes and the risk rating. This is a hypothesis; the facts don't prove cause.
- **Coverage gap:** The 12 FIN-seeded customers have no SCM data, so delivery can't be assessed for them. Win rates are missing or based on few deals for many accounts (e.g., 0% or 100%).

## Evidence

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Infineon | FIN,SAL,SCM,WCP | 60.4 | $621,305 | $1,157,091 | 94.4 | High / 2 |
| GlobalFoundries | FIN,SAL,SCM,WCP | 65.5 | $756,615 | $2,213,667 | 92.4 | Medium / 0 |

Pinnacle Water also has the largest open pipeline ($7,118,699; weighted $4,253,140, SAL) alongside 105 days-to-pay.

- SCM figures are demo enrichment.
- Sales order values shouldn't be compared with SCM order counts.

## Actions

1. **Infineon:** Run a joint delivery-and-dispute review before pursuing its $2.4M weighted pipeline.
2. **Collections:** Escalate SK Hynix and Great Plains, and benchmark payment terms against the more than 90-day norm.
3. **Delivery:** Target OTIF recovery at SK Hynix and GlobalFoundries, where late cost is highest.
4. **Pinnacle Water:** Check its credit position before closing new deals.

| SAL | Opportunity, Sales Org, Sellable Product | None |

   - Journal Entry to GL Account, Cost Center and Legal Entity

# Cross-App Identity: Findings and Recommended Actions

**Direct answer:** Legal entities are reliably conformed. Customer and supplier identity is not. Most cross-app customer and supplier links depend on a **deterministic demo crosswalk** (the six apps share no keys). The heaviest dependency is in Spend, where **245 supplier records fold into 25 golden suppliers**. Treat any cross-app customer or supplier figure as demo-grade until it is replaced with MDG / match-merge output.

## Evidence (crosswalk summary)

| Entity | App | Match method | Records → Golden |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legal Entity | FIN, WCP | exact code | 3 → 3 |
| Legal Entity | PPL, SPD | exact name | 3 → 3 |
| Legal Entity | SCM | regional mapping (demo) | 3 → 3 |
| Customer | FIN / SCM | seed record | 20 → 20 / 8 → 8 |
| Customer | SAL, WCP | rank-based demo crosswalk | 40 → 20 each |
| Supplier | FIN, WCP | seed record + shared vendor key, folded (demo) | 19 → 19 and 31 → 25 each |
| Supplier | SCM | seed record | 6 → 6 |
| Supplier | SPD | rank-based demo crosswalk | 245 → 25 |

## What stands out, and why

- **Legal entities are solid.** They match 1:1 by code or name in FIN, WCP, PPL and SPD. SCM is the exception: it relies on a demo regional mapping.
- **Customers fold 2:1 in Sales and Working Capital.** Each has 40 records mapped to 20 golden customers, using rank ordering rather than real attributes.
- **Spend has the largest fold.** Its rank-based mapping averages about 10 records per golden supplier, so a wrong rank would misattribute spend at scale.
- **FIN and WCP supplier rows are identical.** This suggests a shared vendor master. The "folded" part (31 → 25) is demo logic.
- **Coverage gaps.** The facts show no Sales legal-entity mapping and no People customer or supplier mapping. They don't say whether those are needed.

No governed_concepts were provided, so no governed definitions are quoted here.

## Actions

1. **Fix Spend suppliers first.** Replace the SPD rank-based crosswalk with MDG / match-merge output, matching on tax ID, name and address.
2. **Validate the folding.** Have procurement master-data owners confirm the 31 → 25 vendor-key fold in FIN and WCP.
3. **Firm up SCM legal entities.** Replace the demo regional mapping with an exact company-code mapping.
4. **Rebuild Sales/WCP customers and flag downstream metrics.** Re-match the 40 → 20 customer records on real attributes. Until then, label cross-app customer and supplier metrics as resting on demo identity.

# Cross-App Lineage Analysis: Golden Identities Rest on Demo and Non-BDC Sources

**What stands out:** the golden records (company, customer, supplier) are seeded only by demo enrichment or the Supply Chain knowledge graph. Transactional facts in five of the six apps come from SAP BDC standard data products. Sales is the exception: its CRM opportunities and customers come from a CRM export. Cross-app identity therefore depends on the demo crosswalk, not on governed SAP master data.

**Evidence** (lineage facts: 6 apps, 6 BDC products, 29 sources)

| App | BDC-product source (rows) | Non-BDC sources that feed enterprise identity |
|---|---|---|
| FIN | Journal Entry 10,300; Supplier Invoice 500; Cost Center 45 | AR aging (demo, 3,868) → GOLDEN_CUSTOMER |
| SAL | Sales Orders 558,011 | CRM customers 3,189 (CRM export) → CUSTOMER_MEMBER |
| PPL | Core Workforce 1,500 | — |
| SPD | Purchase Order 3,000 | Supplier risk (demo, 245) → SUPPLIER_MEMBER |
| WCP | Journal Entry 10,300 | DIM_COMPANY (demo, 3) → GOLDEN_COMPANY; DIM_SUPPLIER (demo, 50) → GOLDEN_SUPPLIER |
| SCM | none (BDC-shaped native tables) | KG_NODE 3,642 → GOLDEN_CUSTOMER / GOLDEN_SUPPLIER |

**Why it matters:**
- **Shared source:** FIN and WCP read the same 10,300-row Journal Entry product. Their figures should therefore reconcile.
- **Supply Chain coverage:** Supply Chain has no BDC product, and its operations objects (OPS_EXT) are demo enrichment. These include equipment health, serial genealogy and order fulfilment, and they reach DT_SUPPLIER_360, DT_CUSTOMER_360 and DT_COMPANY_360.
- **Not true shares:** the SAP_BDC_* databases here are standard databases, not BDC Connect shares. They are read through L1 passthrough views.

**Actions**
1. **Re-seed golden records from SAP master data.** Rebuild GOLDEN_COMPANY, GOLDEN_CUSTOMER and GOLDEN_SUPPLIER from governed SAP master data before any production use. Until then, treat all cross-app customer and supplier figures as demo-crosswalk dependent.
2. **Add a FIN-to-WCP reconciliation check** on the shared Journal Entry source. It should catch drift between the P&L and working-capital KPIs.
3. **Flag demo-derived metrics.** Tag supplier risk, AR aging and all SCM OPS_EXT metrics as demo-derived in the semantic view and in agent answers.
4. **Move to real BDC Connect shares.** Replace the SAP_BDC_* databases with shares, and land Sales CRM data via a BDC product if one exists. This makes lineage come natively from OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES.

# Component Lot in the Enterprise Ontology: Structure and Gaps

**Direct answer:** These facts describe the ontology's structure only. They contain no lot counts, inspection results, spend or invoice values. What stands out is how the model is wired: **Component Lot (Supply Chain, SCM) reaches the rest of the enterprise only through Supplier**. Several governance gaps limit cross-app tracing.

**Why: the propagation path**
Component Lot -supplied by-> Supplier. From Supplier, these governed relationships connect to other apps:
- Legal Entity -buys from-> Supplier
- AP Invoice -payable to-> Supplier (WCP)
- Supplier -in category-> Spend Category (SPD)
- Local Supplier -same as-> Supplier

A lot problem can therefore be traced to payables and spend. Cross-app supplier identity depends on the **demo crosswalk**, and SCM uses demo enrichment.

| Observation | Evidence (governed model) |
|---|---|
| Model size | 27 concepts: 19 Enterprise-owned, 8 reused from Supply Chain; 36 relationships; 52 representations |
| No Lot→Material link | Definition says "lot of a BOM component", but no Component Lot→Material relationship exists. |
| System Serial not governed | Named in the Component Lot definition (N:N) but not among the 27 concepts. |
| Purchase Order (SPD), Opportunity (SAL), Journal Entry / GL Account / Profit Center (FIN) are isolated | They have only IS_A links or none, with no tie to Supplier, Customer or Legal Entity. |
| Definitions narrower than usage | Party is defined as "an external organisation", yet Employee is a Party. Transaction "covers Sales Order", yet AP/AR Invoice, PO, JE and Opportunity are also Transactions. |
| Asymmetry | Local Customer -member of-> Legal Entity, but Local Supplier has no equivalent relationship. |

**Actions**
1. Add Component Lot -is lot of-> Material, and govern System Serial, so lot "blast radius" (VW_ONT_LOT_BLAST_RADIUS) can be traced to products and orders.
2. Add Purchase Order -placed with-> Supplier and Opportunity -for-> Customer, so Spend and Sales join through golden parties.
3. Widen the Party and Transaction definitions, or re-parent Employee, so the definitions match how the concepts are used.
4. Replace the demo crosswalk and SCM demo enrichment with production data before relying on any cross-app lot or supplier analysis.
